questions.skill: Make formal constructions with a variety of tools and methods
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: You have no compass, only a straightedge and a strip of paper. Describe how to copy segment AB onto line ℓ starting at point C, and explain why the copy is exact.
questions.prompt_markup: You have no compass, only a straightedge and a strip of paper. Describe how to copy segment AB onto line ℓ starting at point C, and explain why the copy is exact.
questions.correct_answer: Lay the strip along AB and mark the positions of A and B on its edge. Move the strip to ℓ, put the A-mark on C along ℓ, and mark the point at the B-mark: that is D. The strip carries the same length without measuring, so CD = AB.
questions.grading_note: Any valid method using a strip (or string) to transfer the length without reading a ruler, with the reason.

questions.skill: Make formal constructions with a variety of tools and methods
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Describe how to construct the perpendicular bisector of segment AB by folding paper, and explain why the crease is the perpendicular bisector.
questions.prompt_markup: Describe how to construct the perpendicular bisector of segment AB by folding paper, and explain why the crease is the perpendicular bisector.
questions.correct_answer: Fold so that A lands exactly on B and crease. The fold is a reflection that maps A to B, so by the definition of a reflection the crease is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent method and reason (the fold matches A onto B; a reflection line is the perpendicular bisector of PP′).

questions.skill: Make formal constructions with a variety of tools and methods
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: You have a pencil, a pin, and a piece of string, but no compass. Describe how to construct an equilateral triangle on segment AB, and explain why it works.
questions.prompt_markup: You have a pencil, a pin, and a piece of string, but no compass. Describe how to construct an equilateral triangle on segment AB, and explain why it works.
questions.correct_answer: Tie the string to the pin so the length from pin to pencil is AB. Pin it at A and draw an arc; pin it at B and draw an arc; the arcs cross at C. AC = BC = AB because the string length did not change.
questions.grading_note: Any valid string method that keeps one fixed length, with the reason.

questions.prompt: In dynamic geometry software, describe how to construct the line through P parallel to line ℓ so that it stays parallel when P or ℓ is dragged, and explain why a line drawn "by eye" is not a construction.

questions.correct_answer: Use the parallel-line tool (or construct a perpendicular to ℓ through P, then a perpendicular to that line at P). The software keeps the defining relationship when points move; a line placed by eye is not tied to ℓ and stops being parallel when anything is dragged.
